sources.title: The La Bastida fortification: New light and new questions on Early Bronze Age societies in the western Mediterranean
sources.institution: Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona Research Portal; Antiquity
sources.locator: Public abstract, paragraphs 1–2; journal metadata: Antiquity 88(340), 2014, pp. 395–410, DOI 10.1017/S0003598X00101073. Only the abstract was read.
sources.originalChronology: The article dates the stone fortification to 2200–2100 cal BC.
sources.scopedClaim: Stone walls and towers defended a major Argaric political and economic centre in southeastern Spain. The authors interpret the design as a possible response to changing warfare and weapons; they do not establish a particular siege or foreign origin.
sources.reuseTerms: Reference only; no source prose or images redistributed

sources.title: Archaeological Excavation at La Bastida 2018 (April-June): Fieldwork Report
sources.institution: Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona Research Portal
sources.locator: Public abstract, paragraph 2; English abstract in the bibliographic record. The report's full text was not read.
sources.originalChronology: The report provisionally places the hydraulic complex in the earliest settlement phase, about 2200–2025 BC, alongside the original fortification construction. This is a broader phase assignment, not an exact construction date.
sources.scopedClaim: The broader preliminary phase supplies a chronological qualification for the original fortification. No separate hydraulic event or claim of the world's earliest conduit is selected.

sources.title: Vana-Lähis-Ida ajalugu 3500–2000 eKr. Mesopotaamia ajalugu kiilkirja tekkest kuni Uus-Sumeri riigi languseni
sources.institution: University of Tartu Press; public copy hosted by the Estonian Research Council
sources.locator: Sazonov, Espak and Johandi (2015), printed p. 141, PDF page 141, paragraph immediately before section 2.2.9. Text extracted from an ordinary download of the same public PDF after a web size-limit error; no visual page inspection claimed.
sources.originalChronology: The authors explicitly place Utuhegal's defeat of the Gutians and their commander Tirigan around 2120 BC. This date is not calculated from a regnal span.
sources.scopedClaim: Utuhegal, king of Uruk, defeated the Gutians and Tirigan. The authors identify a surviving literary account of the battle. Details of Tirigan's subsequent death and the next dynasty are excluded.

sources.title: Babylonia, c. 2120–1800 B.C., Chapter XXII, The Cambridge Ancient History
sources.locator: C. J. Gadd, public Summary, first paragraph under The Third Dynasty of Ur. Print edition 1971, chapter pp. 595–643. Only the public summary was read.
sources.originalChronology: The summary describes the expulsion and Uruk's briefly restored kingship. The chapter title's date span is not used as an independent date for the battle.
sources.scopedClaim: Utuhegal's expulsion of the Gutians restored Sumerian kingship to Uruk for a brief period. This supports regional political significance without adopting the source's celebratory language.

date.displayEn: 2200–2100 cal BC; broader preliminary phase c. 2200–2025 BC
date.noteEn: The 2014 article dates the fortification to 2200–2100 cal BC. A 2018 report provisionally associates its original construction with the wider earliest settlement phase, c. 2200–2025 BC. Neither gives an exact construction year.

events.summaryEn: Walls and projecting towers guard a narrow entrance to La Bastida, a major political and economic centre of Argaric society in southeastern Spain. Their design may reflect changes in warfare and weapons; it does not identify a particular attack.

review.reviewedBy: Codex independent source and English check

events.selectionNote: A notable defensive building programme at an important Argaric centre. The evidence supports importance 1; the site's prominence does not by itself establish a major regional event.

date.noteEn: Sazonov, Espak and Johandi date the victory to around 2120 BC. This is an approximate date in their chronology, not an exact battle year.

events.summaryEn: Utuhegal, king of Uruk, defeats the Gutians and their commander Tirigan. The victory restores Sumerian kingship to Uruk for a brief period.

review.reviewedBy: Codex independent source and English check

events.selectionNote: A major regional military and political reversal: Utuhegal's victory briefly restored Sumerian kingship to Uruk. Importance 2 reflects the change in regional sovereignty.
